summary.prose: A trivial change now starts with an ISSUE record, like a small bugfix. Triage routes trivial work to the issue stage; the ISSUE records that it is a change rather than a defect and is worded that way. Approving any ISSUE hands the next stage the ISSUE's own hash, and build refuses a no-design build without one, so no new work can end up without its ISSUE. The 16 existing trivial builds that have none get an ISSUE through a repair rule, and their Stories are then completed or held by the existing completion rule.

api.name: routeForSizeClass

parameters.name: magnitude
parameters.purpose: Required for bugfix only; ignored otherwise, as today.

returns.meaning: For 'trivial': { startStage: 'issue', standalone: true, needsPlan: false, producesLld: false } (was startStage 'build'). Every other tier is unchanged.

postconditions: No tier returns startStage 'build'; build is always reached from an approved head.

api.name: buildNextCall
api.signature: buildNextCall(result: TriageResult, focus: string, repo: string, specHash?: string): TriageDone['nextCall']

returns.meaning: For 'trivial': insrc_workflow_step { phase:'start', workflow:'issue', focus, params: { standalone: true, storyTitle, storySpec: focus, sizeClass: 'trivial', magnitude: 'small', kind: 'change', triageRationale } }. A bugfix issue call carries kind: 'defect'. The '(standalone-trivial)' build call is no longer emitted.

postconditions: The trivial nextCall starts the issue workflow, never insrc_build_step.

api.name: finalizeIssue

parameters.name: intent
parameters.purpose: The issue run; intent.params carries magnitude and now kind.

returns.meaning: The stored ISSUE meta carries kind when params.kind is 'defect' or 'change', beside magnitude. Absent params.kind stores no kind (read as defect).

errors.condition: params.kind present but neither 'defect' nor 'change': the ISSUE is not written.

postconditions: A trivial-change ISSUE is stored with kind 'change' and magnitude 'small'.

api.name: nextAfterIssue

returns.meaning: magnitude 'small' (a small bugfix or a trivial change): insrc_build_step { phase:'implement', target:'(standalone-bugfix)', standalone: { standalone: true, sizeClass: 'trivial', epicHash: issue.meta.issueHash, focus: scope } }. magnitude 'sized': the design.story call with params.epicHash: issue.meta.issueHash added.

errors.condition: issue.meta.issueHash missing or not 16 hex characters.

postconditions: Every emitted call names the ISSUE's hash as its work item.

api.name: handleStandaloneImplement

returns.meaning: Unchanged for a call whose epicHash names an approved head.

errors.condition: A no-LLD standalone call with no epicHash; the focus-derived hash is no longer minted.
A no-LLD standalone call whose epicHash has no approved ISSUE.

preconditions: standalone.epicHash names an approved ISSUE (no-LLD) or an approved standalone LLD (small).
postconditions: No standalone build is created without a head.

returns.meaning: kind 'change' renders '## What was asked', '## Why', '## Change'; absent or 'defect' renders '## Reproduction', '## Root cause', '## Fix intent' as today.

api.name: runRepair
api.signature: runRepair(repo: string, mode: RepairMode, options?: RepairOptions): Promise<RepairReport>

returns.meaning: A new rule, 'backfill-issue', runs before units. The preview lists one change per standalone trivial BUILD with no DEF, ISSUE or LLD head. repair writes for each an ISSUE (kind 'change', magnitude 'small', body title and request from the BUILD's focus, why from its triage rationale or 'not recorded', change from its summary) under the BUILD's own hash, anchored at the BUILD's epicCreatedAt, approved by the migration actor with the reason 'backfilled for a trivial build approved before ISSUE-c5b49ff953a9a295'. The existing units and settle steps then create the units and complete or hold each Story by the completion rule; a BUILD that is not approved is not settled. Each write is reported under step 'backfill-issue'.

errors.condition: Unchanged: the plan lists files that cannot be repaired.

postconditions: A second repair lists no backfill-issue change.
No headless standalone trivial BUILD remains after repair.

dataModelChanges.details: Optional kind: 'defect' | 'change'. Absent means 'defect', so every stored ISSUE keeps its meaning and rendering. Written by finalizeIssue from params.kind, and by the backfill as 'change'. Body field names and the four-field validator are unchanged.
A no-LLD standalone build must carry epicHash naming an approved ISSUE; the focus-derived hash is no longer minted.
Repair gains the rule 'backfill-issue' and the step of the same name, ordered before 'units' so the new ISSUE heads anchor the units it creates.

errorCases.scenario: An agent calls insrc_build_step for a no-LLD standalone build without epicHash (an old steering copy or a hand-written call).
errorCases.detection: handleStandaloneImplement finds ctx.epicHash undefined for a no-LLD call, where it used to call standaloneEpicHashFromFocus.
errorCases.response: Return BuildStepError 'no-identity' naming the fix (triage, approve the ISSUE, build with its hash). Nothing is written.
errorCases.userImpact: The build waits for an ISSUE; no headless record is created.

errorCases.scenario: A no-LLD standalone build names an epicHash with no ISSUE, or with a pending ISSUE.
errorCases.detection: Admission reads the ISSUE head for the hash and finds it missing or not approved.
errorCases.response: Refuse with 'no-head' (missing) or the existing unapproved-upstream refusal (pending), naming the ISSUE id.
errorCases.userImpact: The ISSUE is approved first; the build then proceeds.

errorCases.scenario: An approved ISSUE reaches the advance without a usable issueHash.
errorCases.response: Throw; the approval's followOn reports bugfix-advance ok:false.
errorCases.userImpact: The ISSUE stays approved; the agent sees the failed advance instead of a call that would build headless.

errorCases.scenario: An issue run is started with params.kind that is neither 'defect' nor 'change'.
errorCases.detection: finalizeIssue validates params.kind before building the meta.
errorCases.response: Return a schemaFailure; no ISSUE is written.
errorCases.userImpact: The run is corrected and resynthesized.

errorCases.scenario: The backfill fails part-way (a write error after some ISSUEs are committed).
errorCases.detection: The repair step throws; the runner records stoppedAt as 'backfill-issue'.
errorCases.response: The report lists the ISSUEs already written and the remaining changes; later steps do not run. A second repair writes only the rest.
errorCases.userImpact: The user re-runs repair; no ISSUE is written twice.

migration.stateBefore: Triage routes trivial work straight to build (routeForSizeClass returns startStage 'build'; the triage nextCall is insrc_build_step '(standalone-trivial)' with no epicHash). Build mints a work-item hash from the focus for a no-LLD call. The issue-approval advance emits its build and design.story calls without the ISSUE's hash. finalizeIssue stores only magnitude from the run params. A headless trivial build cannot complete its Story because requireEpicAnchor reads only the head. The steering block calls a standalone BUILD record a trivial change's ledger entry (lines 231, 341-342, 463, 536, 557). 16 headless standalone trivial BUILD records exist (15 approved, 1 draft), none with a STORY record.
migration.stateAfter: Triage routes trivial work to the issue stage (sizeClass trivial, magnitude small, kind change). finalizeIssue stores kind; the ISSUE renders change wording for kind 'change'. Approving any ISSUE hands the next stage the ISSUE's hash. Build refuses a no-LLD call without an epicHash naming an approved ISSUE. Approving a trivial BUILD completes its Story under the ISSUE. The steering text says trivial work starts with an ISSUE. After one repair run, each of the 16 old BUILDs has a backfilled ISSUE, and its Story is completed, held or (for the draft) left unsettled by the completion rule.

migrationSteps.action: Add optional meta.kind ('defect' | 'change') to IssueArtifact; absent reads as defect. finalizeIssue stores params.kind and refuses an unknown value; the renderer and the issue.capture prompt use change wording for 'change'. Stored ISSUEs are untouched.
Make nextAfterIssue put the ISSUE's hash into the emitted build call (standalone.epicHash) and design.story call (params.epicHash), refusing an ISSUE without a 16-hex issueHash.
Flip routeForSizeClass('trivial') to startStage 'issue' and change the triage nextCall to start the issue workflow with sizeClass trivial, magnitude small, kind change.
Make the standalone no-LLD build refuse a call without epicHash (no-identity) or whose epicHash has no approved ISSUE (no-head), replacing the focus-derived hash.

Update the steering block at lines 231, 341-342, 463, 536 and 557 so trivial work and a small bugfix start with an ISSUE and the code-review packet pins it; refresh assets/steering-block.md through the plugin's sync-assets.

Add the repair rule and step 'backfill-issue', ordered before 'units': repair-preview lists one change per headless standalone trivial BUILD; repair writes its ISSUE (kind 'change', magnitude 'small', from the BUILD's focus, triage rationale and summary, under the BUILD's hash, anchored at its epicCreatedAt) approved by the migration actor with the reason recorded.

After deployment, back up .insrc/artifacts, .insrc/journal and docs, run repo.convert repair-preview on this repository and check that it lists 16 backfill-issue changes, then run repair and read result.written, held and failed. Stories are completed or held by the completion rule; the draft BUILD's Story is not settled.

migration.backwardCompat: IssueArtifact gains an optional field; old ISSUEs read and render as before, and an old client renders a change ISSUE with defect headings (wording only). The triage nextCall for trivial changes shape (issue workflow instead of build); agents follow nextCall verbatim, and the steering text changes in the same release. insrc_build_step now refuses a no-LLD standalone call without epicHash: a caller relying on the minted hash gets a no-identity error naming the issue stage, instead of a headless build. Small (LLD) standalone builds are unchanged. RepairStep and the repair report gain 'backfill-issue' entries (additive). Step 7 writes records and cannot be undone except by restoring the backup.

alternativesConsidered.name: Issue stage first, with a change kind, and a repair backfill
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Triage routes trivial to the issue stage; the ISSUE records a change kind; approval advances to build carrying the ISSUE's hash; build refuses a headless trivial build; a repair rule backfills ISSUEs for the existing headless builds.
alternativesConsidered.approach: routeForSizeClass('trivial') returns startStage 'issue' (producesLld false) and buildNextCall starts the issue workflow with sizeClass 'trivial', magnitude 'small', kind 'change'. finalizeIssue stores meta.kind ('defect' | 'change'; absent reads as defect) beside magnitude. The renderer and the issue.capture prompt use change wording for kind 'change'. nextAfterIssue puts the ISSUE's hash in the build call (standalone.epicHash) and the design.story call (params.epicHash). The standalone no-LLD build refuses a call without epicHash or whose epicHash has no approved ISSUE, instead of minting a hash. For the existing records, repair gains a backfill-issue rule: repair-preview lists one change per headless standalone trivial BUILD; repair writes an ISSUE (kind 'change') from the BUILD's focus and triage rationale under the BUILD's hash, anchored at the BUILD's epicCreatedAt and approved by the migration actor with the reason recorded; the existing units and settle steps then complete or hold each Story by the completion rule. Steering and guide text change to match.
pros: Every new trivial change and small bugfix gets a person-approved ISSUE, the user's rule.
Story completion needs no anchor change: the ISSUE is the head.
Closes the small-bugfix route to a headless build.
The backfill reuses repair's preview, report and completion rule instead of a separate script.
cons: One approval stop before every trivial build.
The 16 backfilled ISSUEs are system-written after the fact; the migration actor and reason make that visible.

alternativesConsidered.name: Issue stage first, neutral wording, no kind
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same routing and backfill as a1, but every ISSUE is reworded to fit both defects and changes instead of carrying a kind.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Routing, the advance carrying the ISSUE's hash, the build refusal and the repair backfill are as in a1. Instead of a kind field, the capture prompt and the rendered headings become neutral for every ISSUE ('Problem or request', 'Cause or motivation', 'Intended change').
cons: Rewords every defect ISSUE and loses its reproduction / root-cause framing.
Readers cannot tell a defect from a change.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on ac2: rewording every ISSUE degrades defect records to avoid one optional field.

alternativesConsidered.name: Build writes the ISSUE itself
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep trivial routed to build; build's implement phase writes a system-approved ISSUE head from the focus before it starts.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Triage keeps startStage 'build'. When a standalone trivial build has no head, implement writes an IssueArtifact (kind change) from the focus and triage rationale under the build's hash, approved by the system, then builds. The existing headless builds are backfilled the same way as a1.
pros: No extra approval stop for trivial work.
cons: Every future ISSUE for trivial work is system-approved, never reviewed by a person.
Build writes a design-stage record, mixing stage responsibilities.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac5 and the person-approved trace rule for all future work.

alternativesConsidered.name: Anchor fallback only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Leave routing as it is; let Story completion take the anchor from the BUILD record's stamp.
alternativesConsidered.approach: requireEpicAnchor falls back to the work item's BUILD epicCreatedAt when there is no head. Trivial work stays headless; approving its BUILD completes its Story.
pros: Smallest change; existing headless builds could complete with no new records.
cons: No ISSUE record: the trace is still lost, against the user's rule.
Leaves the small-bugfix advance building headless.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Only ac4 is met; the trace stays lost.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The trivial path after the fix: triage starts the issue stage, the user approves the ISSUE, the advance hands build the ISSUE's hash, and approving the BUILD completes the Story under that ISSUE.
